comment: The use of the International Patient Summary as a meaningful minimum for cross-border exchange is valuable. However, a generic patient summary may not contain the profession-specific or contextual meaning needed for continuity in every pathway. A minimum summary can become a ceiling if countries and implementers do not have governed extension rules and tests for preserving additional clinically essential content.

public.text: The use of the International Patient Summary as a meaningful minimum for cross-border exchange is valuable. However, a generic patient summary may not contain the profession-specific or contextual meaning needed for continuity in every pathway. A minimum summary can become a ceiling if countries and implementers do not have governed extension rules and tests for preserving additional clinically essential content.
public.suggestedRevision: Clarify that IPS is a bounded shared minimum rather than a complete representation of care. Require governed national and professional extensions where necessary, without breaking the common core; document inclusion/exclusion rules and terminology bindings; and test that clinically significant content outside the base IPS- such as care needs, functional status, communication requirements, professional judgements, interventions and follow-up plans- can be preserved and exchanged when relevant.
